subject: Post-demo recap: FinFlux auth & SDK onboarding — service accounts, rotation, and routing
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Ella Torres <ella@finflux.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@finflux.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: auth, SDK & next steps (FinFlux)

Hi Ella / Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the FinFlux POC scope.

Summary of what we covered
- Use case: real-time transaction enrichment + user risk scoring; embeddings for similarity search + reranker for precision on high-value transactions.
- Integration paths: server-side SDK (recommended) for synchronous scoring; light client tokens for safe UI features.
- Auth options discussed: OAuth2 delegated flow vs service account with short-lived JWTs + KMS-backed signing. Security briefly prefers short-lived creds.
- Routing: single regional endpoint (us-west) initially, with fallback to a lower-cost model for non-critical batch work.

Requested items from FinFlux (what we need to move to a demo POC)
1) Security contact + required whitepaper checklist (SOC2 scope, key rotation policy)
2) Which identity approach they prefer (OAuth2 user tokens or service account for server-to-server?)
3) A test dataset (sample transaction IDs + PII-stripped payload) and expected QPS during demo hours

Proposed immediate next steps (my ask)
- Ella: share security contact and the SOC2 scope doc by EOD Thu (we can start mapping evidence).
- Samir: confirm if you can accept service account flow with our recommended short-lived JWTs (we provide rotation tooling) or if you need OAuth2 with your IdP.
- Redwood: we’ll send an SDK onboarding checklist and a draft rotation plan; schedule a 45-min integration walkthrough targeted next week.

Attachments: I’ve attached the FinFlux_SDK_Onboard_Checklist.xlsx and a short draft rotation plan.

If this looks right I’ll schedule the walkthrough for next Tue/Wed.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | developer-first inference platform
From: Ella Torres <ella@finflux.com>

Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@finflux.com>, security@finflux.com
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: auth, SDK & next steps (FinFlux)

Vivek — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Security contact: cc'd team is security@finflux.com (Jared Miller will take lead). They asked for an outline of the short-lived JWT flow (how keys are minted, rotation cadence) and any KMS integrations.
2) Preference: our engineering team prefers service accounts for server-to-server calls. Our IdP supports JWT assertion flow and we can accept signed tokens from Redwood if they meet our TTL and rotation constraints.
3) QPS: initial demo target = 30 rps sustained, peak 75 rps; batching ok for non-real-time enrichment.

We attached a link to our internal compliance questionnaire. Jared, please advise on additional artifacts you need.

Can we do the integration walkthrough on Tue 31 Mar 09:00 PT? That works for the engineers here.

Thanks,
Ella
Senior Product Manager, FinFlux
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap: auth, SDK & next steps (FinFlux) — internal action items

Team — forwarding FinFlux's reply. TL;DR: they prefer service accounts + short-lived JWTs and want our rotation plan + KMS details. Action items below.

Internal asks
- Lauren: can you own producing the short-lived JWT spec and a recommended rotation cadence (30m/1h/24h options) and call out implications for KV cache and session affinity? Deadline: Fri EOD.
- Marissa: please prep a lightweight demo script showing SDK init with service account flow (node + python) and token refresh handler. Include a note on embedding/reranker config for 30 rps baseline. Deadline: Mon.
- Vivek: I'll take procurement path — push for a 3-month POC contract (commit for reserved capacity) and draft SOW. Also loop Legal for any SAL/PO requirements.

Bits to include in the rotation doc (suggested)
- Minting model: Redwood issues time-limited JWT signed by our HSM; FinFlux validates signature and TTL.
- Rotation: support automatic key rotation with JWKS endpoint; recommend 1-hour key rollover for production, 24-hour for demo POC.
- Revocation: immediate revocation via blacklist TTL and short token lifetimes.
- Fallbacks: if KMS unavailable, fallback to pre-signed delegated tokens with reduced scope and rate limits.

I’ll coordinate Legal for contract language on key custody and SLAs.

—Ben
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
